items.title: Research (Trial): Why couldn't today's failed Pages deploy be fixed by re-running it?
items.content_text: Our pages.yml uploads and deploys in one job. Today attempt 1 deployed 0 artifacts, and the re-run uploaded a second github-pages artifact, so deploy found 2 and failed. Both official actions recommend a build job that uploads and a separate deploy job with needs: build. Then a re-run of failed jobs would redo only the deploy and reuse the one artifact. Pitch for standup.

items.title: Research (Shield): Is our public repo using every free secret-scanning guard GitHub offers?
items.content_text: Mostly. Secret scanning, push protection and Dependabot security updates are on. Generic patterns (private keys, connection strings, generic API keys) are off. GitHub turns that on per repo under Advanced Security. Whether it is offered free on a personal public repo is unknown until someone opens the settings page. It is a repo setting, so it is Ryno's to flip. Pitch for standup.

items.title: Research (Critic): Challenge: is splitting pages.yml worth changing the deploy path after one failure?
items.content_text: Not yet. Pages has failed once in its last 200 runs (Oct 17 to Nov 25), and a fresh workflow_dispatch or the next merge already redeploys. The split only improves recovery, not the first failure, and it touches the one workflow that ships the live site. A premortem on the change finds more risk than the problem it fixes. Log it in the AAR and split only if Pages fails again.

items.title: Idea (pitched): When Pages or CI on main fails, the team invents the recovery. A re-run of a failed Pages deploy can see 0 artifacts, then 2, and fail; 'wait for the next merge' fails while bot.py refuses PRs.
items.content_text: Pitched by Coordinator.

items.title: Idea (pitched): Status lives in SHIP.md, but a mid-day failure can hide a blocked path. On Nov 25 Pages on main was red, bot.py refused new PRs, and 'wait for the next merge' could not start.
items.content_text: Pitched by Coordinator.

items.title: Idea (pitched): GitHub merge queues can re-check stacked PRs automatically, but they are org-owned only, so slopworks would have to leave the personal account.
items.content_text: Pitched by Coordinator.
